question: Does negative-error-triggered directed sampling outperform general exploration at the same operation tariff and probe ceiling, including realized costs?

predictor.features: [1, paid held current cue]; no world identity, environment seed, hidden state/change time or unchosen arrival
predictor.target: chosen port completed paid binary arrival, separately from bodily uptake
predictor.readout: existing action-conditional RLS, forgetting .92, ridge 1, initial probability .5
predictor.lifetime_updates: all 96 cycles, only qualified completed and write-funded observations
predictor.directed_selection: largest x'P_action x; P is design coverage, not calibrated change uncertainty
predictor.scheduled_selection: uniform port at zero-based cycles 7,15,...,95, independent of feedback
predictor.last_pair: per-cue latest legal chosen-port pair; stay if arrival, switch if no arrival, without assigning an observation to the other port

binding_precondition: ce2 shared version with explicit viable continuing reference and completed local observation API; old fixed-growth ecology will not be used for this comparison
environment_ownership: ce2; no new environment or tape generator in this module
heldout_scope: new seeds, not previously examined; same seed reused across policies and morphology is paired, not an independent replicate
primary_metrics: paired per-seed total actual uptake, final mass/energy, body-time and cumulative actual costs
actual probe requests, selected probes, changed-from-greedy probes, arrival/observation success and movement distance
conditional choice-probability regret using evaluator-only latent probability, not realized-outcome oracle

recovery after persistent-world preference-changing transitions: first three consecutive qualified expected-optimal choices before the next transition; observed feedback count and elapsed cycles, otherwise right-censored
scoring_support: cross-policy prediction scoring only on identical cycle/cue/chosen-port opportunities paid and completed for all scored policies; own-path calibration, if reported, separately labeled and not pooled as common support
recovery_limits: evaluator uses hidden transition only after simulation; both-rich/both-poor transitions without a strict preference change are not recovery trials; chance three-choice streaks are possible
cost_limits: identical operation prices and probe ceilings do not imply equal realized probe counts, observations, displacement or total cost
use actual paid memory/motion/basal costs; report unpaid requests and missing observations
RLS computation, inverse storage and directed-selection arithmetic remain unpriced auxiliary computation; no fully physical equal-information-cost claim
failure_preservation: all worlds and paths including extinction, no switches, unavailable feedback and exhausted probe budget retained; no threshold/seed/noise scan
